title: New-section artwork review
artDirection: Match the supplied ORIGINAL TerminalVibes artwork exactly in visual style: near-black forest and warm brown shadows, aged golden brass, dark green glass, weathered wood, small areas of warm aged parchment, softly luminous green monospaced terminal text, large antique gold serif headings, moss, ferns and tiny fireflies. Use the same richly rendered natural hermit crab with intricately fitted brass shell details. This is a mature, tactile, cinematic botanical workshop, not a cartoon. Match the references’ restrained exposure and warm palette. Keep the explanation spacious and readable. Do not introduce blue-charcoal, cyan, bright white backgrounds, a new palette, or a different illustration medium.
guardrails: Commands, paths, keyboard shortcuts, labels, and before/after results are welcome and expected when they teach the concept. Supply their exact text in the brief, render it legibly, and verify spelling, syntax, and technical relationships against the lesson. Do not replace meaningful text with blank surfaces or decorative pseudo-writing.
Rich illustration is supporting evidence, never the only explanation. Match the visual checks for the concept.
Keep anatomy, light sources, reflections, object counts, folder identities, and transformation direction internally consistent.
Produce an actual distinct image for each alternative, not five crops or recolors of one composition. Do not select or replace any course illustration without the user choosing it.

reviewNotes: Current scope: only the ten new teaching concepts listed in reviewScope. Keep all existing course artwork. The owner ended the replacement-art calibration and requested the exact original course style.

concepts.title: Two routes to the same file
concepts.purpose: Show absolute and relative paths as two ways to describe one destination.
concepts.visualBrief: Teach one idea: an absolute path and a relative path can reach the same file. Create one spacious folder diagram, two directly labeled routes, and one current-location marker. Root / leads through home, vibe, and garden; garden branches to notes.txt and photos. Place both route labels next to the diagram. The title and short subtitle establish the idea. Preserve the original’s intricate craftsmanship in materials and a small guide crab, with restrained botanical framing and ample open space.
visualChecks: Draw the folder hierarchy once: / → home → vibe → garden, then branch to notes.txt and photos. Mark photos as You are here. notes.txt is the single destination.

Trace the absolute route from / through home, vibe, and garden to notes.txt. Trace the relative route from photos up to garden, then down to that same notes.txt. Carry both route colors all the way to the target, using parallel tracks on the shared final edge. Arrows must agree with these directions.
Use exactly the supplied teaching text. No extra slogans, decorative writing, repeated diagram, terminal transcript, shortcut legend, or additional explanatory panel in this particular figure.
Make path strings large and fully legible. Keep two dots and the slash in ../notes.txt. Separate connectors, labels, and decoration so they do not overlap.

Keep substantial open space around the diagram. Use the original’s mature mechanical hermit crab at a small supporting scale. Avoid crowds of props and ornamental boxes competing with the route comparison.
Place photos directly below garden and notes.txt to the right of garden. The amber route must visibly touch garden before continuing to notes.txt; no direct shortcut from photos to notes.txt.
concepts.altSuggestion: One folder diagram shows an absolute route from root and a relative route from the current photos folder reaching the same notes.txt file.

sourceRefs.alt: Paths shown as routes through a branching garden.
sourceRefs.caption: A path can start at the root or at your current folder.

concepts.title: Check assumptions before copying
concepts.purpose: Link argument validation, source checks, fresh destination checks, copying, and result evidence.
concepts.visualBrief: A readable three-stage workflow on one wide brass-framed display: Check, Copy, Verify. The Check area contains three short prerequisite lines. Copy has one command and the qualifier that it must succeed. Verify has a readback command and its one-line result. A quiet crab inspects the copied note. No dense full script or maze of error branches.
visualChecks: Show stage order Check then Copy then Verify. No success label appears before Copy.
The quoted source and destination must remain intact and ordered correctly. The verify example reads the actual copied seeds.txt file; basil is output, not another command.
This is a workflow excerpt, not a complete standalone script. Do not suggest copying guarantees verified contents or automatic rollback.
concepts.altSuggestion: Link argument validation, source checks, fresh destination checks, copying, and result evidence.

concepts.teachingText:
Title: Copy with checks
1. Check
Two arguments
Source folder exists
Destination is new
2. Copy
cp -R -- "$source" "$destination"
Continue only if copying succeeds.
3. Verify
cat "practice copy/seeds.txt"
basil
